name: Nikawiy
description: A star 107 parsecs away, 4.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: radius 4.104 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 8.448 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.057) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: effective temperature 4861 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.022)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.38 from 2024A&A...691A..53S; the 11 published values span log g 3.38 to 3.6, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 74961: distance 106.896 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.026), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 107 parsecs away, 4.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 8.448 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,861 K, so 4.104 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 74961: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 136418 b
quotes.card: HD 136418 b, also known by its proper name Awasis, is an extrasolar planet orbiting the G-type star HD 136418 approximately 320 light years away in the constellation Boötes It has a notable orbit, staying within the known habitable zone.
quotes.introduction: It also has a star with a very similar temperature to the Sun.
